A 37-year-old female presents to the emergency department with episodic back pain radiating to her
abdomen that began yesterday, rating it 10/10 during episodes. Her medical history includes asthma,
anxiety, and previously treated chlamydia. She takes fluoxetine. Laboratory results show: Hematologic:
- Hemoglobin: 14 g/dL - Hematocrit: 40% - Leukocytes: 8,500 cells/mm³ (normal differential) - Platelets:
225,000/mm³ Serum: - Na■: 140 mEq/L - Cl■: 100 mEq/L - K■: 4.9 mEq/L - HCO■■: 24 mEq/L -
BUN: 22 mg/dL - Glucose: 89 mg/dL - Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL - Ca²■: 10.0 mg/dL - AST: 11 U/L - ALT:
11 U/L Urinalysis: - Color: amber - Nitrites: negative - Na■: 12 mmol/24 hours - Beta-hCG: positive -
Red blood cells: 11/hpf What is the most appropriate diagnostic test for this patient's likely condition?
Answer Choices: (A) Urinalysis with microscopy (B) Serum lipase and amylase (C) Pelvic examination
with cervical cultures (D) Renal ultrasound (E) CT scan with contrast (F) Complete blood count with
differential (G) Abdominal ultrasound (H) Transvaginal ultrasound (I) MRI of the abdomen and pelvis
(J) Urine culture
